title: Mistakes table

rows.why it looks bad: The effect teaches an incorrect safe/unsafe boundary.
rows.how to spot it: Overlay authoritative geometry through the full active interval.
rows.fix: Correct the primary border before changing decoration; check every variant. [industry practice: ES-S01]

rows.why it looks bad: Prominence stops predicting consequence.
rows.how to spot it: Show ordinary/critical/ultimate events together and ask which matters.
rows.fix: Reassign relative hierarchy; trim ordinary peaks rather than endlessly enlarging the ultimate. [inference from ES-S02]

rows.why it looks bad: The eye follows decoration instead of collision.
rows.how to spot it: Pause and identify the damaging part.
rows.fix: Demote trail value/opacity/detail and clarify the head. [industry practice: ES-S04]

rows.why it looks bad: Meaning and motion direction become ambiguous.
rows.how to spot it: Remove each layer individually and compare identification.
rows.fix: Keep components with a specific role; replace conflicting silhouettes. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Internal structure and nearby targets disappear.
rows.how to spot it: Inspect normal and grayscale captures with bloom toggled.
rows.fix: Reduce broad glow first; localize the peak and preserve dark/light structure. [inference]

rows.mistake: Pretty in isolation, invisible in play
rows.why it looks bad: Preview background concealed a context problem.
rows.how to spot it: Replay in actual maps/cameras with opponents and UI.
rows.fix: Adjust contrast/shape or stage support, then retest; more saturation is not always sufficient. [industry practice: ES-S07, ES-S09]

rows.why it looks bad: The primary shape becomes shimmer or noise.
rows.how to spot it: View at real projected size during movement.
rows.fix: Select a coarser silhouette, shorten small debris tails or remove tertiary detail. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Equal rates obscure acceleration and release.
rows.how to spot it: Plot size/speed/value over time and inspect main transitions.
rows.fix: Retune the dominant parameter first; preserve deliberately constant projectiles. [inference from ES-S07]

rows.mistake: Extra swelling before an instant impact
rows.why it looks bad: A response reads as late or soft.
rows.how to spot it: Compare gameplay contact timestamp with the visible peak.
rows.fix: Start at a suitable energetic flipbook frame or choose another asset; do not move the gameplay hit casually. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Complexity collapses into one unreadable mass.
rows.how to spot it: Solo the core and compare the combined first peak.
rows.fix: Offset only secondary motion/dissipation while preserving contact alignment. [industry practice: ES-S09]

rows.why it looks bad: The player may keep avoiding a harmless area.
rows.how to spot it: Review the final active tick alongside the remaining visual.
rows.fix: End the semantic hazard cue; retain only clearly different residue if useful. [inference]

rows.mistake: Uniform opacity fade on an asset needing breakup
rows.why it looks bad: The silhouette can look like a flat card being switched off.
rows.how to spot it: Watch the tail against both light and dark surfaces.
rows.fix: Select a breakup flipbook or size/shape tail; retain simple fades when they read better. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Variants imply different reach, intensity or direction.
rows.how to spot it: Compare extremes of randomized settings.
rows.fix: Randomize ornamental parameters inside tested bounds; lock semantic geometry and event timing. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Vocabulary loses reliability.
rows.how to spot it: Ask new players to classify unknown examples.
rows.fix: Define colour plus shape/motion roles and correct exceptions. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Feedback consumes control or visibility.
rows.how to spot it: Aim/navigate during the effect rather than watching a reel.
rows.fix: Lower/remove the troublesome layer and offer reduced camera effects. [inference]

rows.mistake: Late body-hit effect appears on the head
rows.why it looks bad: Correct simulation looks incorrect.
rows.how to spot it: Frame-step a moving/crouching target with latency telemetry.
rows.fix: Use body-part-specific confirmation/attachment only after testing occlusion trade-offs. [industry practice: ES-S18]

rows.why it looks bad: An impressive shader cannot clarify the event sequence.
rows.how to spot it: Replace appearance with simple grayscale parts.
rows.fix: Fix event shape/timing before restoring polish. [industry practice: ES-S10, ES-S09]

rows.mistake: A laboratory number becomes an aesthetic default
rows.why it looks bad: The task/display/population changed.
rows.how to spot it: Inspect each numeric field’s source and context.
rows.fix: Keep study outcomes in evidence fields; obtain game-specific test bounds. [inference]

rows.mistake: Calling a small p-value a large design gain
rows.why it looks bad: Statistical significance does not give magnitude or external validity.
rows.how to spot it: Check effect-size unit, confidence interval, game/sample and actual contrast.
rows.fix: Report the numeric effect and scope; do not promise a retention percentage.

rows.why it looks bad: Unpredictability can be meaningless.
rows.how to spot it: Player sees different colours but cannot learn anything useful.
rows.fix: Keep variation decorative or connect it to interpretable gameplay state.

rows.why it looks bad: Separates consequence from action.
rows.how to spot it: Compare earliest visible contact with audio and gameplay event.
rows.fix: Keep sync anchor fixed; vary tails/secondary details instead.

rows.mistake: Treating 25% as a whole-screen flashing allowance
rows.why it looks bad: Wrong geometry for WCAG’s visual-field criterion.
rows.how to spot it: Look for denominator and viewing-distance assumptions.
rows.fix: Use visual-field analysis and correct standards-aware tooling.

rows.mistake: A safety warning replacing a fix
rows.why it looks bad: Exposure can precede a player’s ability to disable the effect.
rows.how to spot it: Known failures still ship behind a splash screen.
rows.fix: Redesign failure and validate the composite output.

rows.why it looks bad: Lower decoration also deletes essential information.
rows.how to spot it: Play reduced-effects mode without sound.
rows.fix: Preserve or replace the semantic cue with a stable readable one.

rows.why it looks bad: People and contexts vary.
rows.how to spot it: Only simulation has been checked.
rows.fix: Use redundant signifiers, customization and actual player testing.

rows.mistake: Authoring timestamps treated as output sync
rows.why it looks bad: Display/audio pipelines add different delay.
rows.how to spot it: Code says simultaneous but a capture shows separation.
rows.fix: Measure emitted audio and displayed frames on target hardware.

rows.mistake: Using emission cap as scene budget
rows.why it looks bad: Often fails under overlapping effects and large transparent sprites
rows.how to spot it: Count seems legal but on-device GPU frame time spikes
rows.fix: Budget visible area/concurrency and measured CPU/GPU cost, preserving essential cue

rows.why it looks bad: Skips designed buildup or jumps straight into dissipation
rows.how to spot it: Event begins on inconsistent visual states
rows.fix: Disable random start for semantic one-shots; vary approved secondary elements instead

rows.why it looks bad: Smoke and volume disappear against bright backgrounds; overlap washes out hierarchy
rows.how to spot it: Inspect against bright stage and grayscale
rows.fix: Normal blending for obscuring mass; additive only for luminous portions

rows.why it looks bad: Muddies silhouette and increases overdraw
rows.how to spot it: Solo/mute each layer and name what information changes
rows.fix: Keep one primary read; remove redundant layers before adding detail

rows.mistake: Increasing sheet frames without checking cell resolution
rows.why it looks bad: More temporal detail can mean blurrier individual drawings
rows.how to spot it: Inspect per-cell artwork size and close-up phone capture
rows.fix: Choose fewer useful cells or a better-fitting aspect ratio; verify actual resident detail

rows.why it looks bad: Teleport streaks, stale particles or persistent glow appear
rows.how to spot it: Interrupt/reacquire rapidly and inspect the first new frame
rows.fix: Clear history, reset properties and callbacks; respect outstanding lifetime/TimeScale

rows.why it looks bad: Recipe cannot be implemented as written or substitution changes its meaning
rows.how to spot it: Property/class absent from current public API
rows.fix: Specify an honest approximation or request another approved asset; no invented API

rows.why it looks bad: A large flourish can contradict a minor outcome or hide that nothing changed; this is a design diagnosis, not a measured universal law.
rows.how to spot it: Compare the claimed importance with the actual state change; mute sound and remove tertiary layers.
rows.fix: Rebuild the primary contact/state cue, then add only a layer with a distinct job. [inference]

rows.why it looks bad: Uniform speeds and diffuse edges can fail to show where force was transferred.
rows.how to spot it: Scrub first contact and follow-through; check whether heavy pieces move like fine dust.
rows.fix: Concentrate contact timing and separate mass motion from decorative tails; test the revised feel. [inference; ES-S09]

intro: Diagnosis should identify the moment and symptom, then name a concrete change and a retest. These fixes are hypotheses constrained by the cited principles, not automatic guarantees of a better effect.
